content.overview: BNS s. 122 — Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt on provocation.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt on provocation. BNS restatement of IPC 334 / 335. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 334 / 335. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 122 is the rule on “Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt on provocation”. The section provides that (1) Whoever voluntarily causes hurt on grave and sudden provocation, if he neither intends nor knows himself to be likely to cause hurt to any person other than the person who gave the provocation, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 122 exists so that “Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt on provocation” has a closed legal test in Chapter VI — Of Offences Affecting the Human Body. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Homicide, organised crime, terrorism, hurt, acid, restraint, assault, kidnapping and trafficking.

The provision in detail
122. (1) Whoever voluntarily causes hurt on grave and sudden provocation, if he neither intends nor knows himself to be likely to cause hurt to any person other than the person who gave the provocation, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both

(2) Whoever voluntarily causes grievous hurt on grave and sudden provocation, if he neither intends nor knows himself to be likely to cause grievous hurt to any person other than the person who gave the provocation, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees, or with both

Essential ingredients
1. (1) Whoever voluntarily causes hurt on grave and sudden provocation, if he neither intends nor knows himself to be likely to cause hurt to any person other than the person who gave the provocation, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both
2. (2) Whoever voluntarily causes grievous hurt on grave and sudden provocation, if he neither intends nor knows himself to be likely to cause grievous hurt to any person other than the person who gave the provocation, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees, or with both

Explanations
Explanation.—This section is subject to the same proviso as Exception 1 of section 101
